regional_overview: The Trump-Xi summit of May 14–15 has produced asymmetric outcomes across Asia-Pacific that are only legible when read together: Japan received prior-consultation status—Bessent stopped in Tokyo before flying to Beijing, and Trump called Takaichi from Air Force One before contacting any other ally, reaffirming the "ironclad" alliance; South Korea converted the summit into an active facilitation role—Lee Jae-myung hosted Bessent and Chinese VP He Lifeng back-to-back on May 13, proposed a Korea-US currency swap to Bessent, and received a Trump call on outcomes; Taiwan received explicit transactional exposure—Trump described pending arms sales as "a very good negotiating chip," the most direct US presidential statement treating Taiwan's security commitments as tradeable since the TRA's enactment. The summit has thus made visible a structural hierarchy in US Asia-Pacific engagement: consultation partner, active facilitator, and bargaining asset occupy different positions, and no single country desk's reporting captures all three. Beneath this diplomatic restructuring, the Iran war's oil shock continues its transmission through regional economies simultaneously: Japan's wholesale inflation hit a three-year high with bond yields at a 29-year high, South Korea's won broke ₩1,500 per dollar with export prices up 40.8% year-on-year triggering what is now the base case for a May 28 BOK rate hike, and Indonesia's rupiah crossed Rp17,500—nominally exceeding its 1998 Asian Financial Crisis low—as Prabowo's dismissal of the crisis as irrelevant to "villagers who don't use dollars" generated multi-institutional economist backlash that is itself a new variable in the currency's market dynamics.

cross_cutting_dynamics.title: Trump-Xi summit produces visible three-tier US engagement hierarchy across Asia-Pacific: consultation partner, active facilitator, bargaining exposure
cross_cutting_dynamics.assessment: The Trump-Xi summit has produced asymmetric outcomes for the three US treaty allies in the region that are only visible when read together. Japan received prior-consultation partner status: Bessent stopped exclusively in Tokyo (not Seoul) before flying to Beijing, and Trump called Takaichi from Air Force One before contacting any other major ally, explicitly reaffirming the 'ironclad' alliance. South Korea received active facilitation status: Lee Jae-myung hosted Bessent and He Lifeng back-to-back on May 13 — one day before their principals met — proposed a Korea-US currency swap to Bessent, pressed He Lifeng for tangible economic results, and subsequently received a Trump call on outcomes. Taiwan received explicit transactional exposure: Trump described pending arms sales as 'a very good negotiating chip' with Beijing, publicly placing Taiwan's security architecture inside US-China bilateral bargaining for the first time since the TRA. These are not three parallel stories about the same summit — they constitute a structural hierarchy in which the US executive is actively differentiating among its Asia-Pacific partners in real time, with Japan elevated, Korea instrumentalized as a bilateral bridge, and Taiwan explicitly subordinated to US-China deal-making. The three country desks each reported on their piece of this architecture, but none of them could see the full shape of it.
cross_cutting_dynamics.significance: The hierarchy is analytically significant because it makes legible the Trump administration's revealed preference structure in the region: alliance reliability is being redistributed rather than uniformly weakened. Japan's prior-consultation status creates an asymmetry with Korea that will test Japan-Korea coordination going forward. Taiwan's transactional exposure, combined with Japan's elevated status, suggests Tokyo is aware of Taipei's vulnerability in ways that may quietly accelerate Taiwan's diversification diplomacy toward Japan. The HIMARS payment deadline at end of May 2026 now falls inside this hierarchy as the first concrete observable test of whether Trump's 'decision soon' converts transactional rhetoric into actual policy change.
cross_cutting_dynamics.weakest_link: All three country assessments are at confidence 4, but TW's assessment rests on what Trump said publicly (well-sourced via Reuters Tier 2) rather than on any revealed structural commitment; the arms-sales-as-chip statement is the most explicit datum, but whether it produces actual policy change remains unresolved ('decision soon'). The hierarchy framing is an analytical inference drawn from reading the three reports together — it is not itself directly sourced.
cross_cutting_dynamics.evidence_against_linkage: The Trump-Takaichi call could be routine diplomatic courtesy following a major bilateral summit rather than a signal of structural differentiation; the Japan Times notes that Lee Jae-myung also received a Trump call. The 'first call' sequence from Air Force One may reflect Takaichi's personal relationship with Trump more than a durable institutional status. Japan's 'prior consultation' claim rests on Bessent's Tokyo stopover being 'Tokyo only' — Seoul was not on that trip, but this may reflect Treasury logistics rather than deliberate signaling. Korea's facilitation role was largely self-created by Lee's proactive scheduling, not bestowed by Washington. Taiwan's arms-sale statement, while alarming, was followed by no immediate action, and multiple US Republican congressmen (Tiffany and Smith) are actively pushing back against it within the US system.
cross_cutting_dynamics.linkage_justification: The three outcomes are not merely contemporaneous — they are sequentially connected through the same diplomatic event (the Trump-Xi summit), the same institutional actors (Bessent, Trump, the US-China bilateral framework), and explicit cross-referencing: the Japan-Korea Andong summit itself is explicitly framed around 'coordinating responses to US-China dynamics,' meaning Seoul and Tokyo are themselves treating the summit as a shared reference point for their bilateral coordination. The mechanism linking all three is the Trump administration's active differentiation among allies in the context of US-China summit management.
cross_cutting_dynamics.competing_interpretation: The apparent hierarchy could reflect short-term tactical positioning rather than a durable structural reconfiguration. Trump's statement about Taiwan arms sales as a 'negotiating chip' may be characteristic negotiating theater rather than revealed policy — a tactic designed to extract Chinese concessions without actually delivering on the threat. If so, Japan's 'prior consultation' advantage is also tactical rather than structural, and the hierarchy could collapse quickly if Trump decides Taiwan arms sales are not, in fact, negotiable.

cross_cutting_dynamics.title: Iran war Hormuz oil shock transmitting simultaneously through three regional economies, producing convergent monetary tightening pressure with differentiated institutional responses
cross_cutting_dynamics.assessment: The Hormuz disruption's oil cost shock is transmitting through three distinct regional economies in the same week, producing parallel but institutionally differentiated responses. In Japan, April wholesale inflation hit its fastest pace in three years explicitly attributed to Iran war oil costs, long-term bond yields reached their highest level in 29 years, and the BOJ's June rate hike case is now materially strengthened — simultaneously with Takaichi's economic advisers publicly resisting BOJ tapering, producing a reported government-central bank conflict. In South Korea, the KRW broke ₩1,500 per dollar, April export prices rose 40.8% year-on-year, April import prices rose 20.2% year-on-year, newly installed BOK board member Kim Jin-ill explicitly stated inflation worries are 'heightening,' and the May 28 BOK meeting is now the base case for a rate hike, not a hold. In Indonesia, oil import cost surge from Brent at approximately $110 is one of three explicitly named pressure vectors driving the rupiah to Rp17,500+, exceeding its 1998 nominal low. Australia is the partial outlier: the Prime Minister confirmed fuel supply is back to pre-Iran war levels, and the budget delivered temporary fuel excise halving — but the RBA-budget monetary-fiscal tension flagged by the AFR suggests the pressure is present even if partially absorbed.
cross_cutting_dynamics.significance: Three simultaneous rate-hike pressures or currency crises in Japan, Korea, and Indonesia — all traceable to the same Hormuz shock — create compounding regional financial conditions. Capital outflows from Indonesia (third consecutive month for Korea, MSCI rebalancing in Indonesia) are occurring in the same window as BOJ and BOK tightening cycles. This dynamic could amplify currency pressure across the region if rate differentials shift and US dollar strength persists. The Indonesia case is most acute: Rp17,500 breaching the 1998 psychological threshold is not merely an economic event but a legitimacy variable for the Prabowo government.
cross_cutting_dynamics.weakest_link: No single country assessment is the weakest link by score — all are at 4. The most analytically fragile element is the ID assessment's causal chain: the Hormuz oil shock is explicitly named as one of three rupiah pressure vectors (alongside US Fed higher-for-longer and capital outflows), meaning the Hormuz link is real but not the sole or primary driver for Indonesia. Macquarie's assessment that frontier downgrade is unlikely and MSCI's own 'constructive' framing of the removals introduce a competing narrative for the Indonesian equity dimension.
cross_cutting_dynamics.evidence_against_linkage: These are three independent national economies responding to a shared external input — the parallel is structural coincidence, not coordination or contagion. Japan's inflation trajectory preceded the Iran war and reflects domestic labor market tightening and import pass-through that would have produced rate hike pressure regardless. Korea's won weakness has multiple drivers including the Samsung strike risk and domestic fiscal-monetary divergence, not only oil. Indonesia's rupiah weakness has a governance dimension (Danantara, MSCI removal, Prabowo communications) that the Hormuz link does not fully explain. The 'parallel' pattern should not be read as a coordinated dynamic — each central bank is responding to its own institutional context.
cross_cutting_dynamics.linkage_justification: The Hormuz disruption is explicitly named as a causal factor in all three economies' inflation and currency dynamics this week. Japan's wholesale inflation spike is attributed by Reuters directly to 'Iran war oil costs.' Korea's import price surge (+20.2% YoY) and KRW weakness are consistent with oil-price pass-through. Indonesia's BI explicitly cites 'oil import costs from Hormuz disruptions' as a pressure vector. The mechanism — oil price transmission through import costs and current account — is economically standard and operates independently through each country's trade structure, making this coincidence driven by shared structural exposure rather than contagion or coordination.
cross_cutting_dynamics.competing_interpretation: Each economy's tightening pressure could be primarily driven by domestic factors — Japan's 29-year bond yield high reflects domestic fiscal dynamics and BoJ normalization trajectory; Korea's ₩1,500 breach reflects Samsung strike uncertainty and presidential AI dividend communications failure as much as oil; Indonesia's rupiah weakness reflects governance concerns (Danantara, MSCI) and chronic current account fragility that predates the Iran war. The Hormuz link may be the presenting cause for media framing rather than the primary structural driver in any of the three cases.

cross_cutting_dynamics.title: Japan-Korea shuttle diplomacy reaches symbolic apex with Andong hometown summit, explicitly framed as coordinated response to US-China dynamics
cross_cutting_dynamics.assessment: The Takaichi-Lee Jae-myung summit in Lee's hometown of Andong (May 19-20) — with near-state-visit honors, described in both countries' reporting as the most symbolically intimate Japan-Korea bilateral meeting to date — is the third meeting in a sustained shuttle diplomacy sequence. Both the Japanese and Korean country desks flag independently that historical disputes are notably absent from the announced agenda, with Hormuz energy alternatives and potential security cooperation foregrounded. Most analytically significant: both the Japan and Korea desks separately note that the Andong summit is being explicitly framed around coordinating responses to US-China summit outcomes — meaning Japan-Korea bilateral coordination is now synchronized with US-China dynamics rather than operating independently. This is an interaction effect with directionality: the US-China summit is shaping Japan-Korea bilateral agenda-setting in real time.
cross_cutting_dynamics.significance: Japan-Korea normalization has historically been episodic and driven by domestic political contingency in both countries. The explicit framing of this summit around US-China outcomes represents a structural maturation: the bilateral is becoming a coordination mechanism for managing third-party dynamics rather than a bilateral grievance-management exercise. If sustained, this could represent the most durable phase of Japan-Korea alignment since the Abe-Park era — not despite historical tensions being absent from the agenda, but partly because of it.
cross_cutting_dynamics.weakest_link: The Korea desk's DA challenge explicitly notes that the MND officially stated it is 'not considering' a bilateral ACSA, yet ACSA is presented in the alignment_diplomatic assessment as 'foregrounded.' This is an analytical inversion flagged in the DA: if ACSA is not actually on the table from the Korean side, one key deliverable of the summit framing may be overstated. The Andong summit sourcing in the Korea desk (Story #13, 1 source) was noted as single-sourced before being corroborated by the Japan desk's independent reporting — the convergence of both desks on the same event raises confidence, but the single-source origin of the Korean report warrants noting.
cross_cutting_dynamics.evidence_against_linkage: The symbolic elevation of the Andong venue (Lee's hometown) may be more about Lee's domestic political signaling ahead of June 3 elections than a structural realignment — visiting foreign leaders in hometowns creates local political credit. The LDP's simultaneously advancing flag desecration criminalization bill and the reigniting comfort women statue controversy (both flagged in the Japan domestic_regime assessment) represent latent friction that the diplomatic ceremony is papering over rather than resolving. The absence of historical disputes from the agenda may reflect deliberate avoidance rather than genuine resolution.
cross_cutting_dynamics.linkage_justification: Both country desks independently confirmed the same summit, the same protocol elevation (near-state-visit honors), and the same explicit framing around US-China dynamics — the Korea Herald and Japan Reuters sourcing are independent Tier 2 confirmations of the same bilateral event. The mechanism is direct bilateral interaction, not parallel coincidence: Takaichi is flying to Andong; Lee invited her. This is the strongest category of regional linkage because it involves a named shared event sourced independently by both desks.
cross_cutting_dynamics.competing_interpretation: The summit's elevation may be driven primarily by Lee's domestic electoral needs ahead of June 3 rather than by a durable Japan-Korea strategic realignment. Takaichi's visit to Lee's hometown creates optics of international validation for a president whose approval has dropped to 61% and whose Seoul polling has narrowed to 8 points. From the Japanese side, the LDP's advancing nationalist legislation (flag desecration) simultaneously with this summit suggests the diplomatic warmth may not survive a single domestic political test on either side.

cross_cutting_dynamics.title: TSMC-JASM Japan integration deepens as a bilateral TW-JP economic-tech interdependence that is now commercially self-sustaining
cross_cutting_dynamics.assessment: JASM (TSMC's Kumamoto, Japan fab) turned profitable in Q1 2026 for the first time — NT$951M profit versus a prior-quarter loss of NT$1.39B — a milestone that both country desks registered but whose bilateral significance is only visible when read together. From the Taiwan side: JASM profitability is part of TSMC's multi-track international expansion, alongside Arizona, with government subsidy receipts falling 98.56% year-on-year (to NT$505M), indicating the Japan fab is now commercially viable rather than subsidy-dependent. From the Japan side: JASM's upgrade to 3nm for the second Kumamoto fab confirms Japan integration is extending to leading-edge nodes beyond mature-node manufacturing. This trajectory — JASM starting at mature nodes, now upgrading to 3nm, with second fab commissioned — represents a deepening of the structural technology anchor between Taiwan and Japan that operates independently of diplomatic cycles. The Andreessen Horowitz first overseas office opening in Tokyo with a defense startup focus adds a Silicon Valley capital vector flowing into Japan's defense-tech ecosystem, which is structurally complementary to the TSMC integration.
cross_cutting_dynamics.significance: JASM's shift from loss to profit in a single quarter indicates the Taiwan-Japan semiconductor integration is past its critical establishment phase and is now operating on commercial logic. This matters regionally because it creates a durable economic interdependence that functions as a stabilizing factor in Japan-Taiwan alignment — regardless of how the diplomatic weather changes around the Trump-Xi transactionalism, the commercial technology anchor is deepening. It also means Japan's silicon exposure is now partly owned rather than purely dependent on import, changing Japan's strategic calculus on Taiwan security.
cross_cutting_dynamics.weakest_link: Japan economic_tech at confidence 4 caps this dynamic. The Japan desk's assessment of JASM's 3nm upgrade rests on a single source (newkerala.com, Tier 3 per the prior week's reporting, confirmed this week) — the Kumamoto upgrade claim has limited independent corroboration in the Japan desk's current sourcing.
cross_cutting_dynamics.evidence_against_linkage: JASM is a wholly-owned subsidiary of TSMC — its profitability is TSMC's corporate outcome, not a bilateral Japan-Taiwan development per se. Japan is a host for TSMC's international expansion strategy, which also includes Arizona; the bilateral framing may overstate the strategic dimension of what is primarily a commercial investment decision. JASM's profitability may reflect favorable FX conditions (weaker yen lowering local costs) as much as structural commercial viability.
cross_cutting_dynamics.linkage_justification: JASM's first-ever profitability is explicitly reported in both country desks this week and represents a shared outcome of the same bilateral investment that both governments have staked diplomatic capital on. The mechanism is direct: TSMC built a fab in Japan, it is now commercially viable, and both the Taiwan and Japan analytical pictures are updated by this outcome. This is not a coincidental parallel — it is the same entity.
cross_cutting_dynamics.competing_interpretation: The JASM profitability milestone may be primarily driven by cyclical AI demand for mature-node chips (used in automotive and IoT applications that JASM produces) rather than by the strategic Taiwan-Japan technology partnership narrative. If AI demand for mature nodes cools, JASM's profitability could reverse without indicating any structural change in the bilateral relationship.

cross_cutting_dynamics.title: Australia and Japan jointly operationalize Indo-Pacific security commitments in the same week: Balikatan Type 88 live fire includes Australian forces while Australia deploys to Gulf
cross_cutting_dynamics.assessment: The Japan Times' Tier 2 confirmation of Type 88 anti-ship missile live fire during Balikatan explicitly names 'U.S., Australian, and Philippine forces' as the joint exercise participants — a detail that appears only in the Japan country desk and is not mentioned in the Australia country desk at all. In the same week, Australia deployed E7-A Wedgetail airborne early warning aircraft and AMRAAMs to the UAE with an explicit Hormuz freedom of navigation mandate. Read together, Australia is simultaneously participating in Japan-led high-end warfighting exercises in the Pacific and conducting its own Gulf operational deployment. Neither desk cross-references the other, but the Japan Times sourcing places Australian forces inside the most operationally significant security threshold Japan has crossed — live anti-ship missile fire on foreign soil — in the same week Australia crosses its own operational threshold in the Gulf.
cross_cutting_dynamics.significance: The joint Balikatan exercise with Type 88 live fire indicates a level of Australia-Japan security integration that is materially more advanced than the bilateral diplomatic framing suggests: Australian forces are participating in an exercise whose analytical significance is being tracked in Tokyo as the demonstration of a new operational threshold (live fire by Japanese SDF on foreign soil, possible Philippines export of the same system). This is a security integration development that is invisible from either country's desk alone.
cross_cutting_dynamics.weakest_link: Australia's security_defense assessment is at confidence 3. The Balikatan participation by Australian forces is drawn from the Japan desk's Japan Times sourcing (Tier 2) — the Australia desk does not mention Balikatan at all this week. The AU security_defense assessment confidence of 3 reflects AUKUS industrial risk and the Edinburgh facility, not the Balikatan exercise. The cross-cutting inference rests on a Japan-desk source that the AU desk independently neither confirms nor contradicts.
cross_cutting_dynamics.evidence_against_linkage: Australian participation in Balikatan is a routine annual multilateral exercise commitment — Australian forces have participated previously — and does not specifically indicate a new level of Japan-Australia bilateral security integration. The AU desk's silence on Balikatan this week may simply reflect editorial prioritization around the budget story rather than analytical judgment that it lacks significance. The Gulf deployment and the Pacific exercise are operationally unrelated: different commands, different strategic objectives, different force elements.
cross_cutting_dynamics.linkage_justification: The linkage is evidenced by explicit naming of Australian forces in the Japan Times' Tier 2 reporting on the Type 88 live fire — this is not an inference but a sourced fact. The analytical value of reading the two desks together is that it reveals a dimension of AU-JP security cooperation that neither desk foregrounds independently. However, the weakness is that Australian participation in Balikatan is not the primary analytical focus of either desk, and the AU desk's non-mention makes it impossible to assess how Australia is processing this exercise's significance.
cross_cutting_dynamics.competing_interpretation: Australian participation in Balikatan alongside Japanese Type 88 live fire may reflect US exercise design decisions (INDOPACOM coordinating who participates in what) rather than a deliberate Japan-Australia bilateral security integration initiative. The Gulf deployment and the Pacific exercise may simply be two independent operational commitments happening in the same week with no structural connection.

dynamics_considered_and_rejected.candidate_dynamic: AUKUS as active cross-cutting regional dynamic this week
dynamics_considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: AUKUS appeared in the AU desk as a confirmatory signal (licence-free environment operational for over a year) but produced no new development this week. Japan and Korea country desks contain no AUKUS references. The AU assessment itself scores this as minor institutional consolidation rather than a posture development. A cross-cutting dynamic requires movement in at least two country desks; single-country confirmatory signals do not qualify.

dynamics_considered_and_rejected.candidate_dynamic: Coordinated Asia-Pacific defense spending escalation driven by shared China threat assessment
dynamics_considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: Japan, Korea, and Australia are all expanding defense capabilities this week, but the mechanisms are entirely different: Japan's 5% GDP figure is an internal LDP deliberation (Japan desk explicitly notes this is not government policy and may be electoral positioning given debt-to-GDP constraints); Korea's KF-21 nearing deployment is a domestic indigenous capability milestone following a multi-decade program; Australia's Edinburgh facility is a sovereign maintenance investment and Gulf deployment is about SLOC/Hormuz, not China. The stated drivers differ: Japan references Chinese military activity in the Pacific; Korea's defense posture this week is dominated by the OPCON transfer timeline gap with the US; Australia explicitly names SLOC disruption and Hormuz. Parallel defense investment driven by three different threat framings and institutional mechanisms is coincidence responding to different conditions, not a coordinated or contagion dynamic. Forcing these into a single dynamic would be apophenia.

dynamics_considered_and_rejected.candidate_dynamic: Regional central bank coordination in response to Hormuz inflation
dynamics_considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: JP, KR, and ID are all facing rate hike pressure or currency stress this week, but there is no evidence of central bank coordination — no joint statements, no shared institutional mechanism (ASEAN+3 or BIS-level coordination), no explicit reference in any country's reporting to other central banks' decisions. Each central bank is responding to its own domestic conditions and institutional mandates. The BOJ and BOK have different rate-setting cycles, different inflation targets, and different exchange rate frameworks. The BOK Governor's BIS board election this week (KR desk) is a coincident institutional signal but the BIS is not a coordination vehicle for rate decisions. Treating this as coordination would invent a mechanism that the evidence does not support. Recorded instead as a parallel coincidence in cross_cutting_dynamics.

dynamics_considered_and_rejected.candidate_dynamic: North Korea as active cross-cutting regional security variable
dynamics_considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: The North Korean women's soccer team's arrival in South Korea (first DPRK athletes in 8 years) is noted in the KR desk, but Unification Ministry officials explicitly cautioned against reading it as a diplomatic thaw. Neither Japan nor Australia makes any reference to DPRK activity this week. The OPCON transfer timeline gap surfaced in KR security_defense does not specifically reference a current North Korean threat trigger. In a week dominated by the Trump-Xi summit and its aftermath, there is no active DPRK cross-cutting dynamic to synthesize.

dynamics_considered_and_rejected.candidate_dynamic: Shared domestic political backlash against ruling parties across multiple countries
dynamics_considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: Australia (Labor primary to 29%, Taylor leads as preferred PM), Korea (Lee approval to 61%, June 3 polling tightening), and Japan (Bunshun smear campaign in Diet debate, protest demobilization) all show ruling party or government political friction this week. However, the causes are entirely different: Australia's is triggered by a specific budget broken-promise narrative around negative gearing; Korea's is driven by the Bloomberg pressure controversy and special counsel bill positioning; Japan's is a mix of scandal management and post-protest cycle dynamics. There is no shared structural driver and no mechanism linking them. Simultaneous political friction in three different democracies reflects the normal volatility of democratic politics, not a regional dynamic. To synthesize these would be to find a pattern in noise.

dynamics_considered_and_rejected.candidate_dynamic: TSMC Arizona as US-Taiwan-Japan trilateral technology architecture
dynamics_considered_and_rejected.reason_rejected: TSMC Arizona (TW desk) and JASM Japan (TW + JP desks) are clearly linked, but Australia has no semiconductor industry dimension in this week's reporting. Attempting to extend this to a trilateral with Australia would require fabricating a connection. The TW-JP bilateral TSMC interaction is captured in cross_cutting_dynamics; extending it to AU has no evidentiary basis this week.

gaps.expected_dynamic: ASEAN-level or regional financial coordination response to simultaneous currency stress in Indonesia and broader regional monetary tightening
gaps.observed: No ASEAN+3 financial mechanism activation, no Chiang Mai Initiative reference, no regional central bank coordination signal across any of the five country desks. Indonesia's rupiah crisis at the historically significant Rp17,500+ level is being managed entirely through bilateral and domestic channels (Bank Indonesia intervention, Prabowo communications). The Korea desk notes BOK Governor Shin's BIS board election but no ASEAN financial coordination.
gaps.assessment: The absence of regional financial coordination in a week when three major Asia-Pacific economies are simultaneously experiencing inflation shock, currency stress, and monetary tightening pressure is structurally notable. Either the regional financial architecture (CMI, ASEAN+3) is not being activated because the conditions do not meet its trigger thresholds, or the architecture is functionally dormant and individual countries are managing independently. Given that Indonesia's nominal breach of its 1998 low would historically have been a significant regional contagion signal, the silence from regional financial institutions warrants monitoring as a possible capacity or legitimacy gap.

gaps.expected_dynamic: PLA post-summit pressure resumption on Taiwan following diplomatic window closure
gaps.observed: Taiwan desk notes PLA air activity dropped to near-zero during the summit window (2 sorties May 13, zero May 16, against a prior baseline of 10-12 daily) and explicitly flags post-summit baseline tracking as the next analytical task. No post-summit PLA activity data appears in this week's reporting for any country desk.
